title: Visibility-first retry contract and smart load-shed for multi-region failover
creator: Maya Chen
description: Standardize retry, timeout and backoff behavior across services and SDKs with a telemetry-first approach to enable safe multi-region failover, deterministic idempotency semantics, and client-driven smart load shedding.
background: We have multiple ad-hoc retry and timeout implementations in services and SDKs that lead to inconsistent behavior during cross-region failovers. This creates noisy retries, duplicated work, and unclear ownership of failure budgets. Incidents in the last 6 months showed spiky hedged fanout and dropped traces, complicating RCA and increasing token cost when hedging fired unchecked.
goal: Deliver a single, observable retry/timeout/backoff contract implemented in JS, Python and Go SDKs and enforced by the runtime. Provide deterministic idempotency headers, a telemetry-driven retry governor in the runtime, and a client-side smart load-shed policy to preserve SLOs during region failures.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a RetryPolicy object with explicit fields: max_attempts, base_delay_ms, jitter_strategy, max_backoff_ms, per_attempt_timeout_ms, hedging_enabled, hedging_budget_ms
Runtime honors a per-route retry contract and exposes an API to return remaining hedging_budget_ms to clients in response headers
Idempotency header format stabilized as 'X-RW-Idemp:v1:<hex>'; runtime deduplicates server-side for 24 hours unless route opt-out
Telem dashboards show hedged_request_ratio, retry_attempts_by_route, client_backoff_adherence, and dedup_hits; thresholds for alerting are configured
During a two-region failover canary, application p95 exhibits <10% degradation and consumer error-budget consumption does not increase beyond the risk threshold in the playbook
Documentation and migration guide published; at least three internal services complete migration in the canary cycle
proposed_solution: Define a canonical RetryPolicy structure (JSON schema) that SDKs must implement and the runtime honors; include default conservative values and allow per-route overrides

Introduce a lightweight hedging protocol: clients may issue a secondary hedged request after hedging_budget_ms has elapsed; runtime returns a hedging_token header with remaining budget to prevent over-fanout
Adopt deterministic idempotency header 'X-RW-Idemp' with versioning; SDKs create v1 tokens by hashing method+route+body+nonce; runtime performs fast dedupe via a sliding window cache

Add client-side 'smart_shed' policy that consults local circuit state + runtime health header to probabilistically drop low-priority requests when downstream latency or error rate crosses configured SLO thresholds
Enhance telemetry: new tracing annotations (rw.retry.attempt, rw.hedge.fanout, rw.idemp.cache_hit), metrics exported to Prometheus and Grafana dashboards, and enriched log context for RCA
Integrate with circuit breaker state so that retries from a client respect server-side open/half-open signals to avoid amplifying failures

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hedging increases cost when misconfigured. Mitigation: conservative default hedging_budget_ms = 50ms and runtime-enforced global hedging quota per-tenant.
Risk: Idempotency header misuse causing incorrect dedupe. Mitigation: provide strong SDK helpers to build v1 tokens and allow route opt-out for non-idempotent endpoints.
Risk: Large-scale rollout amplifies failures across regions. Mitigation: phased canary with per-tenant caps, traffic shaping and automatic rollback triggers tied to SLO burn rate.
Risk: Observability gaps during failover. Mitigation: synthetic litmus tests that exercise hedging paths to ensure traces and metrics are emitted under stress.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge design doc and SDK PRs behind feature flags; runtime feature flag rollout to staging
Week 1: Internal integration tests and end-to-end load tests simulating regional tail latencies
Week 2: Canary with 3 low-risk services in two regions; monitor telemetry for 48h windows
Week 3: Expand to additional services, tune hedging budget and smart_shed thresholds, and run cost-sanity checks
Week 4: Default enable for new routes; migration window for legacy services with opt-out flag and deprecation schedule
